title: What reviewers have written about pay, premiums, cash-outs and nonprofit executive pay
question: What have the Controller, the Board’s budget analyst, the civil grand jury and the City Attorney put in writing about City pay and about pay and bonuses at organizations the City funds?
finding: 8 documents from 2022 to 2026 in the project’s library make a finding or set a rule about pay. On nonprofits the record is specific: the Controller’s cost rules list “Bonuses paid to staff.” as a cost that may not be charged to the City, its audit of one housing provider is headed “More Than $200,000 in Bonuses Were Unplanned and Paid”, and the City Attorney alleged, of payments another grantee had billed to a City grant, that “these stipends were in fact performance bonuses”. On boards, the budget analyst found that the society running the Zoo had not reviewed its chief executive’s performance from 2019 until the chief executive left. On City pay the library holds less: the budget analyst’s account of what the police agreement added, and its finding on sick leave. No report on disk reviews leave payouts on retirement, premium pay citywide or the Retirement System’s pay.
how: Reports in the project’s document library by the Controller, the Budget and Legislative Analyst, the Civil Grand Jury and the City Attorney were searched for the words bonus, premium pay, cash out, vacation pay, sick leave, executive compensation, executive pay and pay raise, and those that make a finding or set a rule about pay were read. Each row gives the publisher’s date, a one-sentence summary, a quotation of at most twelve words checked word for word against the stored text, and the link recorded when the document was downloaded.
limits: These are findings about particular organizations in particular years; they are not findings about anyone named in the other tables, and two of the organizations have since changed their leadership. A suspension order states allegations. A short quotation cannot carry a report’s reasoning: read the page it comes from. The library holds what this project collected, not every report ever issued, and it has none from the Civil Service Commission or the Retirement Board.

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance and Management Audit of the San Francisco Zoo
rows.said: The budget analyst found that the board of the San Francisco Zoological Society, which runs the Zoo under a lease and management agreement with the City, went years without reviewing its chief executive’s performance, and noted that State rules tie any change in a chief executive’s pay to such a review.
rows.quote: “did not conduct a performance review of the CEO between 2019”

rows.document: Updated July 2025: Guidelines for Cost Categorization in Nonprofit Contracts and Grants
rows.said: The Controller’s cost rules for nonprofit contracts and grants mark bonuses and severance paid to staff as unallowable: they may not be charged to the City.

rows.document: Capacity To Serve: Setting Social Services Nonprofits Up for Success
rows.said: The civil grand jury cited HomeRise, a City-funded housing provider, as having covered losses with improper transfers and paid staff bonuses the jury called questionable.
rows.quote: “gave questionable bonuses to staff until it was forced to change leadership”

rows.document: Suspension Order and Counts and Allegations Seeking Debarment Under San Francisco Administrative Code Chapter 28
rows.said: The City Attorney alleged, in an order suspending the grantee Collective Impact, that payments it had billed to a City grant as stipends were performance bonuses, which the grant did not allow. An allegation in a suspension order is not a finding by a court.
rows.quote: “these stipends were in fact performance bonuses”

rows.publisher: San Francisco Budget and Legislative Analyst
rows.document: Performance Audit of Police Dept Overtime
rows.said: The budget analyst’s audit of police overtime set out the pay terms of the police agreement from July 2023 and, separately, found sick-leave use by sworn staff up 77% in five years with patterns it called potential abuse.
rows.quote: “wage increases, retention pay, step adjustments, and signing bonus”

rows.said: The Controller’s audit of HomeRise, a City-funded housing provider, found staff bonuses paid in 2022 that were neither planned nor budgeted, charged in part to properties running deficits.
rows.quote: “More Than $200,000 in Bonuses Were Unplanned and Paid”

rows.said: The same audit found pandemic bonus pay, meant by the City for front-line staff, given to executives and managers and charged to City grants.
rows.quote: “gave at least $11,567 in bonuses to executive and managerial employees”

rows.document: Nonprofit Wage and Equity Survey Report
rows.said: The Controller’s survey of nonprofit contractors found executives at organizations with budgets under $5 million paid a mean of $47.22 an hour against $80.52 at larger ones, and wrote that helping small organizations raise executive pay would have positive equity effects.
rows.quote: “difference in the mean wages of executives in small and large organizations”

rows.document: Public Integrity Investigation at the Department of Building Inspection (City Attorney report, January 18, 2022)
rows.said: The City Attorney’s investigation of the Department of Building Inspection wrote that its former director was given pay raises despite reports that had found favoritism in the department.
rows.quote: “Hui was rewarded with pay raises, despite reports that found favoritism”
